habitat: Flocks near large rivers and marshes, and in woodland and mixed bushveld, hawking from trees and from the ground.
summary: Newman calls it a common summer resident and visitor. The largest bee-eater in the region, with carmine-red body and wings, a blue crown and a pink throat, and a curved black bill. It differs from Northern Carmine Bee-eater by the blue crown and the pink, not blue, throat. The immature has brown upperparts and pale cinnamon underparts with traces of pink. The call is a deep terk, terk. Status and months are left unset because Newman gives both summer resident and visitor. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

research.note: Newman says common summer resident and visitor. Northern Carmine Bee-eater is the comparison and is not in this list. Carmine is not a colour token. Population figures and the Kemp code NB were left unchanged. Status is intra-african-migrant: SABAP1 describes a three-stage migration, with post-breeding dispersal into the Transvaal and departure to equatorial Africa in March.

similar.note: Blue-cheeked Bee-eater is green above, with pale blue cheeks and a rufous throat. It is not carmine.
